title: Storm off the gulf
body: A late-season storm tracks over Richfield County and sits on your site for a day. Crews pull back until the water clears. Without delay-in-start-up cover, the lender freezes construction draws until you cure the paperwork.
bodyVariants: The rain comes sideways for a day and the site turns to mud. Crews stand down until it drains. Unless you carry delay-in-start-up cover, the lender holds construction draws until the freeze is cured.

A storm parks over Richfield County and the cranes go quiet. One of the halls loses ground to the weather. The lender freezes construction draws until the claim is cured, unless delay-in-start-up cover is active.
Lightning on the horizon, water on the pad. The crew chief calls it before lunch. Expect the lender to freeze construction draws until cured unless you carry delay-in-start-up cover.
note: Phase 3: rare and large. Odds 0.04/mo in season while a hall is in pad/steel/shell. Damage = tuning.events.stormDamageShare of the hit hall's costBudget; with builder's risk you keep the flat per-claim deductible and the policy pays the rest, without it cash pays all. insuredDelayMonths +1 only if builder's risk was in force. Sets a draw freeze unless DSU is active. The claim lands on state.claims for the event card.

title: A shock up the supply chain
body: A fire at a parts supplier ripples through the grid-equipment market. Everyone's lead times just got longer, yours included.
bodyVariants: A supplier fire halfway across the country lands on your desk as a revised lead time. Months, not weeks.
The parts market tightens overnight. Your expediter calls it a queue problem. It is now your queue problem.
Grid equipment is suddenly everyone's problem. A pending order of yours slips with the rest.
note: "randomPending" selects uniformly among currently pending transformer/switchgear orders.

title: Not enough hands
body: Fitout crews are scarce across the region this quarter. Your general contractor is stretched thin and it shows in the schedule.
bodyVariants: The GC's phone keeps ringing with other offers. Fitout crews are thin this quarter.
Every job site in the county is hiring the same people. Your fitout crews feel it first.
Reyes warned you about steady crews. This quarter, steady is hard to find.
note: "importCrewsActive" is derived: true while month < flags.importCrewsUntil (set by the importCrews action or the union_pla card). labor_shortfall's own odds drop to 0.05 while flags.plaSigned is true (see union_pla).

title: A rating agency cuts the outlook
body: A regional rating agency trims its outlook on data center campuses like yours, citing power delivery risk. Buyers get a little more cautious.
bodyVariants: An analyst in a tower somewhere trims the outlook on campuses like yours. Exit math gets a little colder.
The agency cites power delivery risk. You have read this paragraph before, in other people's deals.
A one-notch outlook cut. Not a crisis. Not free either.

title: The tenant wants more
body: The Whale's expansion team calls. They want two more halls on your campus, same terms, same you. It is a vote of confidence and a lot more rope.
bodyVariants: The Whale's expansion team has a slide deck and a favor: two more halls, same terms, same you.
The tenant calls before your coffee is cool. They want to double down on the campus.
More halls, same handshake. The Whale's team makes it sound simple. It is not simple.
note: Fires at month 24 if the docket is already approved; otherwise fires the month the docket is approved. Yes: addAskHalls adds 2 halls of 25 MW IT, delivery = last hall's delivery + 9 and +12 months, opens a docket amendment vote in 9 months, and scales senior/equity commitments pro rata. No: declineAsk sets tenant goodwill -20. Failing the amendment vote later cancels the ask halls without a lose.

title: The next generation of racks
body: The tenant's hardware team wants to leap to the next rack generation mid-build. Whether that is free, expensive, or a fight depends on what you are cooling with.
bodyVariants: The tenant's hardware team has a new rack generation and a strong preference for it. Mid-build, naturally.
New silicon, new racks, same delivery date. The tenant's engineers are excited. Your scheduler is not.
The hardware roadmap moved. The tenant wants the campus to move with it.
note: Tier-dependent, resolved inside the chipGeneration effect handler using setup.hallTier: hybrid = no penalty. liquid = choice of retrofit (each undelivered hall +$4,000,000 and +1 month fitout) or decline (tenant -15). air = tenant -15 and asset score -3 unless retrofit at +$15,000,000 per undelivered hall. The handler sets phase=awaitingChoice with tier-appropriate choices; content intentionally leaves choices empty here since they depend on setup, not a fixed list.

title: A dry summer
body: Richfield County is in a drought watch. Your cooling choice is about to matter to people who live downstream of your water permit.
bodyVariants: The county posts a drought watch. Suddenly everyone downstream of your permit is paying attention.
A dry summer, and your cooling choice is a topic at the diner again.
The river gauge is low, and people know whose towers are whose.
note: Deltas come from tuning.cooling.<setup.cooling>.droughtTown/droughtCommission. Evaporative stings the most, dry cooling is immune.

title: A subpoena from the docket
body: Commission Staff wants your internal load forecasts, every draft. You can hand them over or fight the request in front of the commissioners.
bodyVariants: Commission Staff wants every draft of your load forecast. All of them. In writing.
A discovery request lands: internal forecasts, every version. Your lawyer sighs audibly.
Staff is asking for documents you would rather summarize. That is not how discovery works.
note: The trailing "p:0.5" arg means the effect handler applies that goodwill delta with 50% probability in addition to the guaranteed -5.

title: The county assessor comes by
body: Now that something is actually standing, Richfield County wants to talk about the property tax abatement everyone signed off on. It goes fine. It usually does.
bodyVariants: The assessor walks the site, asks about the abatement, and leaves satisfied. A good county meeting.
Now that steel is standing, the county wants to talk taxes. The abatement holds. Everyone nods.
The assessor's visit goes fine. Signed abatements are beautiful things.

title: The lender's engineer flags a draw
body: Your monthly draw request does not match the paperwork on file. Until someone sorts it out, the lender is not releasing funds.
bodyVariants: The lender's engineer does not like the paperwork on this month's draw. No funds until it matches.
A signature is missing somewhere, so the draw sits. The lender is polite and immovable.
Your draw request and the file do not agree. The money waits until they do.
note: Cured by the cureDraw action (1 AP).

title: Fire in fitout
body: An electrical fault sparks a small fire in a hall under fitout. No one is hurt. The hall is a different story.
bodyVariants: A fault in a panel sparks during fitout. The extinguishers work. The schedule does not.
Smoke in a hall under fitout. Everyone is fine. The hall needs work.
One electrical fault, one small fire, one harder week in fitout.
note: Phase 3: rare and large. Odds 0.004/mo during fitout. Damage = tuning.events.fireDamageShare of the hit hall's costBudget, settled like a storm. -2 months of progress, insuredDelayMonths +2 when insured, no draw freeze.

title: The budget line that moved
body: Steel prices moved again and your general contractor wants to talk about a change order. Under a cost-plus deal, that bill is yours.
bodyVariants: Steel moved again. Your GC slides a change order across the table.
The cost-plus clause wakes up hungry. Steel prices are the reason this time.
A budget line twitches upward. Under cost-plus, that twitch is yours.

title: A failed inspection
body: The county inspector walks the site and does not like what they see. Work stops on that hall until it is fixed.
bodyVariants: The inspector walks the hall, stops twice, and starts writing. Work stops until this clears.
A clipboard, a frown, a failed inspection. That hall sits until you fix it.
The county inspector finds what your punch list missed. The hall pauses.
note: Cleared by the fixInspection action.

title: Rates move up
body: The Fed's latest move pushes floating construction rates up. Cap rates follow, a little.
bodyVariants: The Fed moves, your floating rate follows, and the exit math tightens a notch.
Money gets a little more expensive this month. Your senior draw notices first.
Rates tick up. Construction debt does not send a card, it just costs more.

title: Rates move down
body: A softer inflation print gives the market room to breathe. Your floating rate eases, and so does the exit math.
bodyVariants: A soft inflation print, a kinder tape. Your floating rate exhales.
Rates ease. The model looks a little friendlier this month.
Cheaper money, for now. The senior rate drifts down.

title: Millbrook calls a town hall
body: The town wants a night with you, a microphone, and their questions. Showing up costs an evening. Not showing up costs more.
bodyVariants: Millbrook books the VFW hall and puts your name on a flyer. Questions will be asked.
The town wants a microphone, a folding chair, and you. On a weeknight.
A town hall is called. Attendance is technically optional.

title: The Clarion runs a profile
body: Sam Okafor's piece on the campus runs this week. How it reads depends on how the town feels about you right now.
bodyVariants: The Clarion's piece runs above the fold. What it says depends on what Millbrook already thinks.
Sam Okafor's profile of the campus runs this week. The town reads itself in it.
The profile is out. The quotes are accurate. The tone is earned.
note: Automatic, no player choice: if goodwill.town < 40, commission -5; else town +5.

title: The tenant offers to slide a date
body: The Whale's deal team floats an idea: push one undelivered hall's date out a bit in exchange for a small rent break. No hard feelings either way.
bodyVariants: The Whale's deal team proposes a trade: a later date on one hall, a small break on rent.
A friendly call from the tenant: slide one delivery date, shave the rent a touch. Your call.
The tenant offers to move a date. Two months of slack for two points of rent.
note: Accept: the next undelivered hall's delivery and outside months +2, rent on that hall -2%. Decline: no change. Implemented directly in the choice handler (same mechanics as the delaySwap action), since hall-date shifts have no generic closed-set effect.

title: The Governor wants a tour
body: Governor Voss is in Richfield County and wants photos at your site. It is good press, if you can spare the afternoon.
bodyVariants: The Governor's office wants a tour and a photo. The advance team is already picking angles.
Governor Voss is nearby and cameras are available. Your site is the backdrop, if you agree.
A gubernatorial drop-by is proposed. Hard hats will be provided. Yours, specifically.

title: A project labor agreement, on the table
body: The trades council offers a project labor agreement: steady crews, fair terms, a small premium on the budget. Reyes is waiting on your answer.
bodyVariants: The trades council brings a draft agreement: steady crews, fair terms, a small premium.
Reyes lays the agreement on the table and waits. Steady labor has a price.
The council offers a project labor agreement. Your budget notices the premium. Your schedule notices the calm.
note: Signing also drops labor_shortfall's draw odds to 0.05 for the rest of the run via flags.plaSigned (see labor_shortfall).

title: Fire at the transformer plant
body: A fire shuts down the factory building your transformer. The lead time just got a lot longer.
bodyVariants: The factory building your transformer is a smoking roof today. The lead time is a rumor now.
A fire at the transformer plant. Your unit is fine, probably. The queue in front of it is not.
The call comes from the factory: fire, shutdown, new dates. None of the dates are soon.

title: The interconnection study needs another look
body: The utility's planners want to rerun part of your interconnection study after a nearby project changed its load profile.
bodyVariants: A neighboring project changed its load, so the utility wants to rerun part of your study.
The planners found a new wrinkle in the load flow. Your study goes back for another look.
Someone else's project moved, and yours waits a few more months for the rerun.

title: Your equity partner pushes back
body: Your partner has funded calls and bridges for you and wants it back in share or schedule. The more you lean on them, the more often this comes up.
bodyVariants: Your equity partner reads the numbers and the capital calls. Lawyers are mentioned.
Your partner wants a bigger slice or a long pause. Pick the one that costs less.
Every call you made was their money. They want something for it.

choices.label: Concede a bigger share and pay their legal fees
Wait it out (a month of delay and a retainer)

title: Neighbors worry about their wells
body: Families near the site say their wells are running low and point at your cooling towers. Evaporative cooling drinks a lot of water.
bodyVariants: Two families on the county road say their wells are low, and they know where to point.
Well complaints, three of them, all aimed at your cooling towers.
The neighbors' wells are the talk of the feed store. Your towers get the blame.
note: Mitigation: visitCast(town).

title: A heat wave during commissioning
body: A heat wave rolls through right as a hall is ready to commission. Equipment runs hot and tests slip a little.
bodyVariants: Triple digits during commissioning. The equipment runs hot and the tests slip.
A heat wave picks the exact week a hall goes through commissioning. Of course it does.
The thermometer wins a round. Commissioning tests slide a little.

title: The rebate comes through
body: The equipment rebate the Governor's office promised finally clears. It is real money, and it is yours.
bodyVariants: The rebate the Governor's office promised finally clears. Eight figures, real money.
A wire from the state: the equipment rebate. It was worth the paperwork.
The rebate lands. The Governor's office kept its word.

title: A good stretch of weather
body: Clear skies and mild temperatures for weeks. Every crew on site is ahead of where they expected to be.
bodyVariants: Weeks of clear skies. Every crew is ahead of where the schedule says they should be.
Mild, dry, boring weather. Exactly what a job site wants.
The forecast gives you a month of gifts. The crews spend it well.

title: A regional hiring fair
body: The county is running a hiring fair for skilled trades. Sponsoring a booth costs a little cash and buys some goodwill, plus a steadier crew for a while.
bodyVariants: The county fairgrounds fill with tradespeople and folding tables. A booth has your name on it, if you pay.
A regional hiring fair is coming. Sponsoring one is cheaper than a crew shortage.
The county runs a hiring fair. For a small fee, your banner can hang over a booth.
note: While flags.hiringFairUntil is in the future, labor_shortfall's draw odds are reduced by 0.05.

title: A commissioner's term ends
body: One of the sitting commissioners is replaced mid-docket. The new seat starts from the middle, not from whatever you had built up.
bodyVariants: A commissioner's term ends mid-docket. The new seat has no history with you, good or bad.
Turnover at the commission. The new member starts at neutral, because of course they do.
A new face at the dais. Whatever you built with the old one stays with the old one.

title: A favor in the interconnection queue
body: Arcadia Public Power has room to move your study up the queue. They only do that for developers they trust.
bodyVariants: The utility has room in the queue and moves your study up. Trust, it turns out, is a schedule item.
Arcadia Public Power shuffles the queue and your study lands a few months sooner.
A quiet favor from the utility: your interconnection study jumps the line.

title: Water in the building
body: A fitting lets go over a weekend and a floor takes on water. Crews dry it out and re-do the work. It is small, it is annoying, and it is the most common claim on any job site.
bodyVariants: A pipe separates on a Saturday night. By Monday there is an inch of water on the slab and a line of wet drywall.
Rain finds a gap in the envelope before the roof is tight. The crew spends a week pulling wet insulation.
A pressure test goes wrong and a joint fails. No one is hurt. The floor below is a pond.
note: Phase 3 small class: odds 0.02/mo while any hall is under construction. Loss is tuning.events.waterDamageShare of a random active hall's costBudget, always inside the deductible, so the policy pays nothing and it costs the same insured or not. Also -0.5 month of progress on that hall.

title: Copper walks off the site
body: Someone cut the fence overnight and drove off with cable and tools. The sheriff takes a report. Your crew re-orders and moves on.
bodyVariants: A trailer of copper wire leaves the yard after midnight. The gate camera caught a plate and not much else.
Thieves strip a spool of cable from the laydown yard. It is not much money, and it is the second time this year.
A deputy calls at dawn: the lock was cut and the tool crib is empty.
note: Phase 3 small class: odds 0.015/mo while any hall is under construction. Loss is tuning.events.theftShare of a random active hall's costBudget, inside the deductible. No schedule hit.

title: Before the trucks arrive
body: Neighbors want to see the site plan. A small open house costs $100K and adds 5 town trust, which helps permit odds. It does not guarantee approval or speed up construction. You can keep the cash instead.
note: First-campus-only scenario-scheduled choice. No random odds and not globally scripted, so this card cannot draw in other scenarios.

title: A steadier crew for the build
body: A local training program costs $250K. It reduces the base chance of a labor shortage by 5 percentage points for 8 months, with a floor of zero. Shortages can still happen; this does not make ordinary construction faster.
note: First-campus-only scenario-scheduled choice. No random odds and not globally scripted, so this card cannot draw in other scenarios.

title: Your tenant asks for a walkthrough
body: A design walkthrough uses 1 action point next month and adds 6 tenant trust. Tenant trust affects deadline flexibility and sale value. It does not complete work for your crews. Or keep all your points for building.
note: First-campus-only scenario-scheduled choice. No random odds and not globally scripted, so this card cannot draw in other scenarios.
